text: Interactive elements on mobile should have a minimum tap target of roughly 44x44px (iOS) or 48x48dp (Android) to avoid mis-taps, even if the visible icon is smaller — pad the clickable area, not just the icon.

Body text should meet a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against its background (WCAG AA); large headings can go as low as 3:1. Low-contrast pastel-on-white text looks elegant but fails accessibility and readability checks.

Micro-interactions (button hovers, toggles) read as responsive at 100-250ms. Longer transitions (page transitions, modals) feel smooth at 250-400ms. Anything past ~500ms starts to feel sluggish for direct-response UI.
Establish hierarchy through size, weight, and contrast before color — a page that only differentiates importance by color often fails for colorblind users and in grayscale printouts/screenshots.
Generous whitespace around a call-to-action increases perceived importance and click-through more reliably than making the button itself bigger or louder.
Sticky navbars improve navigation on long pages but should shrink or simplify on scroll (hide secondary links, reduce height) so they don't eat too much vertical space on mobile.
A single, visually dominant primary CTA per screen converts better than multiple competing buttons of equal visual weight — secondary actions should be visually subordinate (outline/ghost style).
Pairing one expressive display font for headings with one highly legible, neutral font for body text is a safer default than using more than two font families on a single page.

E-commerce and SaaS hero sections convert better when the primary CTA is visible without scrolling and paired with a single clear value statement, rather than a rotating carousel of multiple messages.
Skeleton screens (gray placeholder shapes matching the eventual layout) are perceived as faster than spinners for content-heavy pages, because they set expectations about what's coming.
An empty state (empty cart, no search results) should explain why it's empty and offer one clear next action, rather than a bare 'no results found' message.
Single-column forms are completed faster and with fewer errors than multi-column forms, because users don't have to decide which field to fill next.

Product/content cards benefit from a consistent internal padding and a single clear focal image; adding a subtle elevation (shadow) on hover signals interactivity without needing extra copy like 'click here'.
True black (#000000) backgrounds cause harsh contrast halos around light text; a dark gray (e.g. #121212-#1A1A1A) is generally more comfortable for extended reading in dark mode.
Progressive onboarding (teaching features as the user reaches them) generally outperforms long upfront tutorials, which are frequently skipped entirely.
Bottom tab bars are more thumb-reachable than top navigation on mobile, especially on larger phones — reserve the top bar for less frequent actions like search or profile.

When a UI adopts a strong theme (e.g. a franchise, retro, or brutalist aesthetic), core usability patterns — button affordance, form clarity, contrast — should not be sacrificed for the sake of the theme; style the surface, not the interaction logic.
Background/ambient animation should stay under roughly 10-15% opacity or movement amplitude in content-heavy screens, so it reads as atmosphere rather than distraction from the actual task.
